english_lines: The man who plots harm against the very one who helped him—
Such a thorough scoundrel will be ruined in the end.
Those sinners who resolve to set a burglar's rod against the very house that fed them
Will have to turn to dust.
notes: `கன்னக்கோல்` is rendered as the burglar's rod/tool used to break into a house, preserving the betrayal image.

english_lines: Bewitched by a guise, desiring in vain,
After the deception is past, if the heart is left in anguish,

source_tamil_lines: பாலை ஊற்றிப் பாம்பை நாம் வளர்த்தாலும் நம்மையே
english_lines: Even if we rear a snake by pouring it milk, it will come
Only to bite us—we will have to strike it dead.
notes: The proverb-like snake-and-milk image is retained directly.

translator_notes: The source's moralizing images of betrayal, disguise and the milk-fed snake are translated concretely rather than abstracted.
Item-level lyric authorship remains unresolved at this booklet-evidence tier; translation does not upgrade attribution.
